patch.value: Core command flag_invocations misclassify valueless booleans as required string values

Command-scoped machine contracts derive several core boolean flags as takes_value:true and value_required:true (for example init --defaults, test --run, --progress, and --fail-on-skipped), contradicting Commander help and executable behavior. Unify core invocation arity with the canonical flag declaration so agents can safely synthesize invocations without scraping human help.

Every core boolean flag reports takes_value=false and value_required=false in command-scoped flag_invocations while value-bearing flags retain truthful required/optional/repeatable metadata.; A parity gate compares executable Commander arity with SDK flag_invocations for every core command and fails on a synthetic boolean/string mismatch.; Compact discovery remains within token budgets and generated contract fixtures, SDK docs, Node/Bun packed acceptance, and exact coverage are updated.
Make machine contracts sufficient and trustworthy for autonomous invocation synthesis
Agents avoid invalid retries and wasted context caused by boolean flags advertised as required strings
Corrects the universal SDK contract used by CLI, MCP, packages, and recursive self-improvement tooling
Packed acceptance for positional/MCP parity reproduced the contradiction on multiple high-use core flags
